quiz.0.question: Why does Nebbiolo perform brilliantly almost exclusively in Piemonte?
quiz.0.options.0: It can only grow in cold climates
quiz.0.options.1: It requires specific marl-calcareous soils, a very late-ripening season and Piemonte's particular fog (nebbia) to achieve full maturity
quiz.0.options.2: It is legally restricted to Piemonte
quiz.0.options.3: It is grafted onto rootstocks that only survive in Piemonte
quiz.0.explanation: Nebbiolo needs Piemonte's marl-calcareous Langhe soils and a specific microclimate to ripen its thick skin fully — even though it has been planted worldwide, it rarely achieves the same heights outside Piemonte.
quiz.1.question: What is Barbera's most distinctive characteristic?
quiz.1.options.1: Naturally high acidity with low tannins — the most food-friendly Italian variety
quiz.1.explanation: Barbera is defined by its naturally high acidity and low tannins — making it ideal with rich, acidic foods like tomato-based pasta. With barrel ageing, it develops considerable complexity.
quiz.2.question: Sangiovese Grosso is principally used in which DOCG?
quiz.2.explanation: Sangiovese Grosso (known locally as Brunello) is the variety used for Brunello di Montalcino DOCG — one of Italy's greatest and most age-worthy red wines.
quiz.3.question: Why is Aglianico called 'the Nebbiolo of the South'?
quiz.3.options.0: It is a light-coloured variety with floral aromas
quiz.3.options.1: Both are late-ripening, high-acid, high-tannin varieties with long ageing potential that only excel in their native region
quiz.3.options.2: It has the same DNA as Nebbiolo
quiz.3.options.3: Both are grown exclusively in the Alps
quiz.3.explanation: Aglianico and Nebbiolo share the same winemaking profile: late ripening, high acidity, high tannins and extraordinary ageing potential — both thriving in their specific volcanic (Aglianico) or marl-calcareous (Nebbiolo) soils.
